content.text:
The snapshot fallback can recursively write itself in hosts that announce widget-state changes, and restored approval cards expose controls that cannot authenticate. Both affect the runtime behavior introduced by this patch despite the focused tests passing.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Avoid re-persisting widget-state events — /Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/mcp-app-chatgpt-rehydrate/packages/owletto/src/mcp-apps/_shared/host.tsx:165-167
  When the host publishes `setWidgetState` changes through `openai:set_globals`, an event containing `widgetState` reaches this branch and immediately calls `persistOpenAiData` again. Because that creates another state object and calls `setWidgetState` again, persisting any result can cause recursive event traffic or a stack overflow instead of mounting the card. Only persist updates originating from `toolOutput` or standard tool results; widget-state restoration should be read-only or deduplicated.

- [P2] Strip capability-gated actions from cached views — /Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/mcp-app-chatgpt-rehydrate/packages/owletto/src/mcp-apps/_shared/openai-compat.ts:45-48
  When a pending approval card is restored from `widgetState` without `toolResponseMetadata`, this returns its original `resolve_lobu_approval` actions while `Provider` initializes `approvalCapability` to null. Approve or Reject then calls `resolveLobuApprovalImpl` without the required capability and always receives a 403, leaving dead mutation controls on the restored card. Persist a display-safe view without those actions, or reacquire a fresh capability before enabling them.
